capabilities: Capture ideas and reading notes as cards in projects, categories, and subcategories
Quick-capture selected text from any note into a new card
Parse pasted citations and generate bibliographies in Academic Mode
Search, preview, compare, and reorganize cards across projects
Export cards as Markdown files with Obsidian frontmatter
disambiguation: Not a Kanban or card view of existing vault notes; cards live in the plugin's own data file until they are exported as Markdown.
extras: Desktop only (Windows, macOS, Linux implied; mobile not supported). All data lives in a single JSON file (.obsidian/index-cards-data.json) with automatic dated backups of the five most recent versions and protection against overwriting a damaged file. Academic Mode is off by default. README includes a table of contents, settings table, and keyboard shortcut list.
motivation: The README says the workflow mirrors physical index cards researchers have used for decades: write it down quickly, keep it organized, move it into permanent notes when ready.
problem: Card-style Obsidian plugins mostly display existing vault notes, leaving researchers without a dedicated scratch space to jot and organize rough working notes before they become permanent notes.

relations.evidence: Copy a citation from Zotero (Edit → Copy as → Bibliography Entry)
a citation parser that reads copied bibliography text from Zotero, Google Scholar, Logos

requires.name: Zotero, Google Scholar, Logos, or another reference manager (for citation parsing)

summary: Card-based research capture workspace that stores ideas and reading notes as virtual index cards in projects and categories, then exports them as Markdown files.
